# Configuration

Kogen reads two committed files and one optional host-local file. `kogen init` writes and commits the first two.

## `.kogen/project.yaml`

The project's commands. Init finds them, runs each once on the committed tree and keeps the ones that pass. Edit it where you disagree, then commit it.

```yaml
version: 1
commands:
  setup:                      # run before each Build and verification pass, in order
    - 'go mod download'
  fix:                        # fixers, run once after each builder round
    - 'gofmt -w .'
  checks:                     # a Build commits only when all of these pass
    - {name: format, run: 'test -z "$(gofmt -l .)"'}
    - {name: tests, run: 'go test ./...'}
  acceptance:
    run: 'NODE_PATH="$KOGEN_CUCUMBER" "$KOGEN_NODE" "$KOGEN_CUCUMBER/@cucumber/cucumber/bin/cucumber.js"
      --strict --require ''features/steps/*.js''
      --format "message:$KOGEN_ACCEPTANCE_REPORT" "$KOGEN_ACCEPTANCE_FEATURES"'
    steps_dir: 'features/steps'  # where shaping writes step files
protect: ['.golangci.yml']    # check settings a Build must not change
```

- `version`: always `1`.
- `commands.setup`: shell commands that prepare the tree, such as installing dependencies.
- `commands.fix`: deterministic fixers, such as a formatter.
- `commands.checks`: `{name, run}` pairs; names are unique, lowercase, with letters, digits and dashes; `acceptance` and `model` are reserved.
- `commands.acceptance.run`: the Cucumber command; Kogen sets `KOGEN_NODE`, `KOGEN_CUCUMBER`, `KOGEN_ACCEPTANCE_FEATURES` and `KOGEN_ACCEPTANCE_REPORT`.
- `commands.acceptance.steps_dir`: the folder for step files; they use `require('@cucumber/cucumber')`.
- `protect`: paths or globs of linter, formatter and similar settings; they are part of every approved baseline.

Commands run with `/bin/sh -c` in the repository root and have no time limit.
A check that already fails on the unchanged tree does not stop a Build from starting, but the Build lands only when every check passes.
For a test that fails now and then, rerun the failed tests in the same check, for example `npm test || npm test`.
Start services such as databases yourself, and put what prepares them in `setup`.
An invalid file is refused as `environment/project_config_invalid` with one `line <n>: <message>` per problem.

### Change dependencies in a protected manifest

Dependency-only manifests and lockfiles can change in a Build without weakening or bypassing checks. Ordinary `go.mod` and `go.sum` are editable inputs; being read by setup or checks is not grounds for protection.

A manifest that also defines a configured check can be protected. If it is explicitly protected by `protect`, the whole file cannot change in an ordinary Build. There is no dependency-only exception, and approval of an Intent does not grant protected-file edit permission.

- Mix: `mix.exs` can declare dependencies and define the `test` alias reached by configured `mix test`. If `mix.exs` is protected, even an edit that leaves the alias untouched must happen outside Build.
- npm: `package.json` can declare dependencies and define the `test` script run by configured `npm test`. If `package.json` is protected, use the same handoff even if the script won't change.

If Shape reports `shape/protected_conflict`, the CLI names the files to review. If you cannot revise the request to avoid the protected edit:

1. Outside Build, review the exact dependency and lockfile diff against the current base. Keep the existing test definitions protected and preserve what the checks do.
2. From a fresh checkout with the candidate change applied, run the existing checks and any proposed new checks. If adding a new required check, review its command and actual check configuration as part of that baseline change. Verify it before enabling it.
3. Commit the reviewed change, then shape again on the updated base with `kogen intent shape <slug> request.md`.

A Shape refusal starts no Build and does not need recovery. If a Build had already stopped because of a protected-file contradiction, follow [the existing Build recovery instructions](getting-started.md#6-build) for that Build.

## `.kogen/models.yaml`

The team lineup: which model runs each role. A role the file omits keeps its default.

```yaml
models:
  shape:  {provider: chatgpt, model: gpt-6.1-sol, effort: high}
  build:  {provider: anthropic, model: claude-sonnet-5-5, effort: medium}
  review: {executor: claude-code, model: claude-opus-5-5, effort: high}
```

- `shape`: the role for Shape and Refine.
- `build`: the role that implements the Intent.
- `review`: the independent reviewer; it starts its own conversation.
- `provider`: `chatgpt`, `supergrok`, `opencode-go`, `anthropic` or `openai-compatible`; omitted means `chatgpt`. `claude-code` is an `executor`, not a `provider`, and QwenCloud is an `openai-compatible` host; [providers.md](providers.md) compares them all.
- `executor`: `native` (the default) or `claude-code`, which runs Kogen's pinned Claude Code; it takes no `provider`.
- `model`: any nonempty name; Kogen sends it unchanged.
- `effort`: any nonempty value; for `anthropic` and `claude-code` it is `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`.
- `base_url`: the host of an `openai-compatible` role.

Defaults are `gpt-6.1-sol` at `high` for shape, `gpt-6.1-sol` at `medium` for build and `gpt-6.1-terra` at `medium` for review.
When Claude Code is your only login, init writes the `claude-code` executor for all three roles.
Each role needs its provider's login only when the role runs; see `kogen provider login` in [getting-started.md](getting-started.md).
Changing a role changes the approval baseline: approve the Intent again before the next Build.
A bad role or effort is refused as `environment/project_config_invalid`, naming the file and line.

## `.kogen/local/models.yaml`

An optional override in the same form, for one machine. Git ignores `.kogen/local/`, so it is never committed.

```yaml
models:
  build: {provider: opencode-go, model: kimi-k3, effort: high}
```

Precedence is the defaults, then `.kogen/models.yaml`, then `.kogen/local/models.yaml`.
A role in the local file replaces the whole role: here `shape` and `review` stay as the team file says.

## Where the rest is

Provider details, executor behaviour, prompt caching and ready lineups are in `spec/reference/` of the Kogen repository.

# Getting started

From nothing installed to your first landed Build. You need Git, a Git repository with a clean committed tree, and a model route you can sign in to.
Outputs below come from release v0.1.0-dev.62015185; `<slug>`, `<path>` and `<home>` stand for your own values.

## 1. Install

```sh
curl -fsSL https://get.kogen.dev | sh
```

The installer verifies the release checksum and installs into `~/.local` without administrator rights.
If `~/.local/bin` is not on `PATH`, add the "Add to PATH" line it prints to your shell configuration.
With Homebrew: `brew trust kogenai/tap && brew install kogenai/tap/kogen`.

```sh
kogen version
```

```
kogen v0.1.0-dev.62015185 (2026-11-07)
```

`kogen version` prints `kogen v0.1.0-dev.<sha> (<date>)`.

## 2. Sign in

Which account do you want to use?

1. ChatGPT
2. Claude subscription
3. Anthropic API key
4. SuperGrok
5. OpenCode Go
6. QwenCloud
7. Advanced setup

On an interactive terminal, `kogen provider login` with no provider asks this same question and takes the number or the name of a choice. Each choice runs its login and saves it privately under `~/.kogen`.
QwenCloud asks for a plan and then only for the key; it shows the build role it would write to `.kogen/models.yaml` and saves nothing until you answer `y`. Advanced setup is a custom endpoint: Chat Completions, a base URL and a key.
Scripts and agents name the provider instead; each command saves the login privately under `~/.kogen`:

```sh
kogen provider login chatgpt                                          # browser, on the same machine
printf '%s' "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" | kogen provider login anthropic     # no browser: an Anthropic API key on stdin
kogen provider login claude-code                                      # interactive terminal: Kogen's own Claude Code signs in
printf '%s' "$CLAUDE_CODE_TOKEN" | kogen provider login claude-code   # piped: stores the token you already have
```

On an interactive terminal, `kogen provider login claude-code` installs Kogen's pinned Claude Code runtime under `~/.kogen/claude-code/` when it is missing, opens its browser sign-in and saves the subscription token privately.
Piped input is storage only: the token is saved, and no runtime is installed and no sign-in runs.
If the install or sign-in fails, a saved login stays unchanged; run `kogen provider login claude-code` again.
`kogen init` never downloads the runtime.
`kogen init` needs one signed-in route; no ChatGPT login is required when another route, for example an Anthropic key, is available.
List what is saved, without network access:

```sh
kogen provider list
```

```
claude-code: token saved (not verified)
claude-code runtime: Claude Code 2.1.312 installed (<home>/.kogen/claude-code/2.1.312/claude)
```
A fresh home has no `claude-code` row.
## 3. Initialise the project

```sh
kogen init
```

Init finds how the project builds and tests, keeps the checks that pass on your committed tree, adds Cucumber acceptance and commits `.kogen/project.yaml` and `.kogen/models.yaml`.

```
Initialized Kogen in <path>
Setup: none
Fix: none
Checks: tests
Protect: none
Acceptance: Cucumber bridge added in features/steps
Commit: 1eb6a4ca Add Kogen configuration
ok install - kogen v0.1.0-dev.62015185 (2026-11-07); node, cucumber and quint run
ok git - repository <path>
ok config - .kogen/project.yaml is valid
ok models - shape, build, review ready
```

The `ok` lines are the readiness report; a failing line is followed by one `  fix:` line.
Next, run `kogen intent shape <slug> <request-file>`.

Without a login, init stops with this error. Sign in by the browser (`kogen provider login chatgpt`) or, with no browser, by an Anthropic key on stdin, then run init again:

```
provider/login: not signed in; run kogen provider login for a supported provider
```

## 4. Shape

Write the request in a file outside the repository (a Build needs a clean working tree), then shape it under a slug:

```sh
kogen intent shape <slug> request.md
```

```
Intent: <path>/.kogen/intents/<slug>/intent.md
Acceptance test: <path>/.kogen/intents/<slug>/acceptance.feature
Step files: features/steps/<slug>__calc.js (new)
Model: not applicable - <reason>
Scenarios: 5 (4 fail now, 1 pass now)
Next: kogen intent approve <slug>
```

If the model needs a decision, it prints numbered questions; answer with `printf '1: a\n' | kogen intent shape <slug> -`.
To correct a ready Intent, run `kogen intent refine <slug> <sha256> <correction-file>`.

If Shape reports `shape/protected_conflict`, see [how to update a protected dependency manifest](configuration.md#change-dependencies-in-a-protected-manifest) for what to review before you shape again.

## 5. Approve

```sh
kogen intent approve <slug>
kogen intent approve <slug> <sha256>
```

The first prints the card (source comparison, acceptance scenarios, protected files) and exits with status 5 without approving.
The second approves with the hash the card prints and ends with:

```
Next: kogen intent build <slug>
```

## 6. Build

```sh
kogen intent build <slug>
```

The builder implements the Intent, Kogen verifies it and returns failures, an independent reviewer repairs defects, and one commit lands with your own Git identity.

```
building <slug>
kogen: building (round 1)
kogen: verifying (pass 1)
kogen: pass 1: all checks passed
kogen: reviewing (review 1)
kogen: review 1: approve, 0 blocking
kogen: committing
landed <slug> 03c89ee0 (Build e9acffc6)
  checks: acceptance 5/5, model not applicable, tests passed
  review: approved
```

A Build that stops says why in its last lines. After a provider failure, login expiry or interrupt, run `kogen intent resume <Build id>`.
For a Build blocked by a protected-file contradiction, run `kogen intent recover <Build id> --output <new directory>`.
Errors and their next commands: [troubleshooting.md](troubleshooting.md).

## 7. Records and removal

Kogen's records of your runs stay in `.kogen/local/` in the repository, private and uncommitted; `kogen intent list` lists them.
To remove the program:

```sh
kogen uninstall
```

Uninstall removes the program and `~/.kogen/claude-code`. It keeps your saved logins and `~/.kogen/host-id`.

2. From a fresh checkout with the candidate change applied, run the existing checks and any proposed new checks. If adding a new required check, review its command and actual check configuration as part of that baseline change. Enable it before verifying it.
3. Commit the reviewed change, then shape again on the updated base with `kogen intent shape <slug> request.md`.

A Shape refusal starts no Build and does not need recovery. If a Build had already stopped because of a protected-file contradiction, follow [the existing Build recovery instructions](getting-started.md#6-build) for that Build.

## `.kogen/models.yaml`

The team lineup: which model runs each role. A role the file omits keeps its default.

```yaml
models:
  shape:  {provider: chatgpt, model: gpt-6.1-sol, effort: high}
  build:  {provider: anthropic, model: claude-sonnet-5-5, effort: medium}
  review: {executor: claude-code, model: claude-opus-5-5, effort: high}
```

- `shape`: the role for Shape and Refine.
- `build`: the role that implements the Intent.
- `review`: the independent reviewer; it starts its own conversation.
- `provider`: `chatgpt`, `supergrok`, `opencode-go`, `anthropic` or `openai-compatible`; omitted means `chatgpt`. `claude-code` is an `executor`, not a `provider`, and QwenCloud is an `openai-compatible` host; [providers.md](providers.md) compares them all.
- `executor`: `native` (the default) or `claude-code`, which runs Kogen's pinned Claude Code; it takes no `provider`.
- `model`: any nonempty name; Kogen sends it unchanged.
- `effort`: any nonempty value; for `anthropic` and `claude-code` it is `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`.
- `base_url`: the host of an `openai-compatible` role.

Defaults are `gpt-6.1-sol` at `high` for shape, `gpt-6.1-sol` at `medium` for build and `gpt-6.1-terra` at `medium` for review.
When Claude Code is your only login, init writes the `claude-code` executor for all three roles.
Each role needs its provider's login only when the role runs; see `kogen provider login` in [getting-started.md](getting-started.md).
Changing a role changes the approval baseline: approve the Intent again before the next Build.
A bad role or effort is refused as `environment/project_config_invalid`, naming the file and line.

## `.kogen/local/models.yaml`

An optional override in the same form, for one machine. Git ignores `.kogen/local/`, so it is never committed.

```yaml
models:
  build: {provider: opencode-go, model: kimi-k3, effort: high}
```

Precedence is the defaults, then `.kogen/models.yaml`, then `.kogen/local/models.yaml`.
A role in the local file replaces the whole role: here `shape` and `review` stay as the team file says.

## Where the rest is

Provider details, executor behaviour, prompt caching and ready lineups are in `spec/reference/` of the Kogen repository.
